subject: Request: temporary SLA amendment & proportional credit model for NovaCast migration
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@novacast.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA ask for migration period (Novacast)

Kim,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We're going into a multi-phase migration of latency-sensitive inference traffic starting Oct 1 and running through mid-November. Given the expected load spikes and DNS cutover risk, procurement and SRE want a temporary relaxation of the standard 99.95% uptime requirement for the migration windows.

Specifically: can Redwood support a temporary 99.5% uptime floor for the months of Oct and Nov, with a mutually-agreed credit calculation tied to observed degraded latency and short-duration interruptions? Procurement also asked for a monthly credit cap so our procurement team can model worst-case exposure.

Attached is the high-level migration schedule. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Kim
Head of Infrastructure Operations
NovaCast
attachments: Novacast_migration_window_schedule.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@novacast.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for migration period (Novacast)

Daniel —

Appreciate the context and the schedule. We're happy to explore a temporary amendment so you can migrate with reduced operational friction. I looped in Marissa (CS lead), Ben (sales/finance), and Aditya (runtime/product) to weigh in on feasibility and commercial guardrails.

Two quick asks while we evaluate:
- Can your SREs share the expected qps profile by week for Oct/Nov? A short CSV is fine.
- Do you expect any production PII/workloads that would require a private deployment or dedicated capacity during the migration?

We'll propose a small set of options (credit model + cap + operational controls) and aim to get back with a formal proposal within 48 hours.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for migration period (Novacast)

Team —

Quick read from CS/ops: we can tolerate a temporary uptime floor reduction if we pair it with three constraints:
1) A monthly credit cap expressed as a percent of committed spend (we typically push for 20% cap in pilot scenarios).
2) A requirement for NovaCast to run critical inference on dedicated capacity or specific pinned model versions during high-risk weeks. That minimizes cross-customer blast radius.
3) Clear telemetry hooks (shared dashboards) so both sides accept measured availability/latency windows.

Aditya — can you confirm whether our current metric extraction supports a weighted credit model tied to observed 1-minute latency spikes vs sustained downtime? If not, what's the engineering ETA?

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask for migration period (Novacast)

Marissa —

We can support a proportional (weighted) credit model that differentiates brief latency degradations from full availability loss. High-level options here:
- Option A (simple): keep uptime percent threshold but prorate credits by duration of unavailability per month; cap by percent of monthly invoice. (quickest to implement)
- Option B (weighted): define three bands — brief latency spikes (1m > threshold), partial degradation (5m sustained elevated error rate), full outage (timeout/retries). Each band maps to a per-minute credit rate. This requires a short telemetry mapping and a runbook for how incidents are classified (we already have incident types used internally). Implementation risk: low; engineering will need to validate the mapping with NovaCast dashboards. ETA: 5 business days to finalize wording and telemetry agreement.

Also: for dedicated capacity checks, we can provide a temporary dedicated pool for the Oct high-risk weeks; we need a firm commit on traffic to size it and an upfront minimum.

Aditya
Head of Platform Product
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@novacast.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, procurement@novacast.com
Date: 2026-09-10T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: temporary SLA amendment & proportional credit model (Novacast)

Daniel —

Thanks for your patience while we pulled internal stakeholders together. Below is our proposal for a time-boxed SLA amendment covering Oct 1 — Nov 30, 2026. Please review and tell us any must-haves we missed. If this looks reasonable we'll prepare a short amendment doc for signature.

Proposal (summary):
- Temporary uptime floor: 99.5% for Oct and Nov 2026 for the services listed in the attached migration schedule.
- Proportional credit model: credits are calculated monthly by classifying minutes into three bands:
  • Band 1 (latency spike): 1 minute windows where p50 latency > 2x baseline and error rate < 1% => credit = 0.05% of monthly invoice per affected 15-minute block.
  • Band 2 (partial degradation): sustained elevated error rate or p95 latency > 3x baseline for >= 5 minutes => credit = 0.25% of monthly invoice per affected 30-minute block.
  • Band 3 (outage): service unavailable or error rate > 50% for >= 5 minutes => credit = 1% of monthly invoice per affected 30-minute block.
- Monthly cap: credits capped at 15% of monthly invoice for Oct and Nov (we can revisit after the pilot).
- Dedicated capacity: for three high-risk weeks (dates listed in your attachment), Redwood will provide a temporary dedicated pool sized to your committed minimum QPS. This requires a 30% committed baseline for the pool during the weeks and will be invoiced as a short-term reserved capacity line item (we'll include estimated cost).
- Telemetry & measurement: both parties will use a shared dashboard and agreed incident classification runbook (Aditya's team will publish the mapping within 5 business days). Measurements from the shared dashboard are authoritative for credit calculation.
- Sunset & reversion: this amendment auto-expires Dec 1, 2026 and services revert to the standard SLA unless a signed extension is agreed.

We attached a sample "proportional-credit-matrix-v1.xlsx" with worked examples against your migration schedule. If procurement is comfortable with the 15% cap and the dedicated pool requirement, we can convert this into a formal amendment and legal redlines.

Next steps:
1) Daniel/procurement: confirm acceptance of the core terms (uptime floor, cap, dedicated pool) or list non-negotiables.
2) Aditya/ops: finalize the runbook and sample dashboard (ETA 5 business days).
3) Ben/finance: I'll need an estimated reserved pool cost to include in the amendment.

Would you like a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the sample calculations?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
